summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with quadriplegia, chronic indwelling Foley catheter, tracheostomy, and GJ tube was admitted for difficulty replacing his Foley catheter at the nursing home. Urology successfully placed a hydrogel Foley catheter in the ED. Urinalysis showed white blood cells and nitrites, and initial white blood cell count was mildly elevated, prompting a single dose of ceftazidime. However, the patient remained afebrile and asymptomatic, and repeat labs showed normalization of white count. Given his history of chronic colonization and lack of infection signs, antibiotics were discontinued. Cultures remained pending at discharge. Chronic medications were continued unchanged, and tube feeds were planned to resume at the nursing home. He was discharged to extended care in stable condition.
